scenes.vo: In January twenty twenty-four, HP's CEO said some of his own customers are a bad investment.

visual.sub:
WHAT HP'S CEO CALLED
SOME OF ITS OWN CUSTOMERS

scenes.vo: His reason: customers who skip HP's own ink, he said, are not worth the investment.

visual.quote: “…if that customer doesn't print enough or doesn't use our supplies, it's a *bad investment.*”
visual.who: Enrique Lores, HP CEO · CNBC interview, Jan 2024

scenes.vo: HP often prices the printer itself close to what it costs to make.

visual.sub:
THE PRINTER ITSELF
ISN'T WHERE HP MAKES MONEY

scenes.vo: In fiscal twenty twenty-five alone, HP's ink and toner supplies brought in ten point nine billion dollars.
A feature called Dynamic Security can block ink that isn't HP's, even ink refilled in an HP cartridge.

visual.headline:
PRINTER FIRMWARE
CHECKS THE CHIP

items.text: Non-HP or refilled ink can be *blocked*

visual.source: Source: HP Dynamic Security policy · class actions filed Jan 2024 (N.D. Cal., N.D. Ill.)

scenes.vo: The printer is the hook. The ink is where the business actually lives.
When the product is cheap, you're not the customer. You're the installed base.

visual.display: When the product is cheap, you're not the customer. You're the *installed* *base.*
